published_statement: Abstract (p.1): 'We present the first general model for subluminal positive-energy, spherically symmetric warp drives; construct superluminal warp-drive solutions which satisfy quantum inequalities; provide optimizations for the Alcubierre metric that decrease the negative energy requirements by two orders of magnitude ... any warp drive, including the Alcubierre drive, is a shell of regular or exotic material moving inertially with a certain velocity. Therefore, any warp drive requires propulsion. We show that a class of subluminal, spherically symmetric warp drive spacetimes, at least in principle, can be constructed based on the physical principles known to humanity today.' Sec 3.1 (pp.9-10): w(r) = (1-(r/Lambda)')/(8 pi r^2) (eq 6); 'for purely positive energy spacetimes, Lambda(r) > 1 in the outside region D_out ... Schwarzschild'; 'any non-trivial truncated spherically symmetric warp drive must contain regions where the energy density is negative'; 'for a subluminal warp drive based on non-exotic matter, the time inside the drive can only pass more slowly than it does for a remote Minkowski observer comoving with the drive. For scale, an Earth-mass shell of 10 meter radius will slow down the rate of time by a small fraction of 4e-4.' Sec 5.2 (p.18): 'the only type of modification to the internal spacetime that is achievable with purely positive energy for spherically symmetric warp drives is slowing down the rate of time inside the craft'; the general axisymmetric positive-energy case 'remain[s] important open questions'. Sec 5.3 (pp.18-19): 'flattening the shape by a factor of 10 would lead to proportionally smaller energy requirements'; optimal shape f = min(r0/r_s, 1) 'reduces the energy requirement for a similarly sized Alcubierre drive by about a factor of three' (App. A.3, eq A.7: E = -(v_s^2/12) Int_{r0}^inf r_s^2 f'^2 dr_s). Sec 5.4 (p.19): 'it is possible to construct non-trivial warp drive solutions with purely positive energy ... While the mass requirements needed for such modifications are still enormous at present, our work suggests a method of constructing such objects based on fully understood laws of physics.'
published_hypotheses: H1 General warp drive (sec 2.1, p.4): asymptotically flat vacuum D_out enclosing a compact curved D_warp of spherical topology enclosing a flat passenger region D_in; stationary, admitting a global Killing field xi aligned with the inner boundary's 4-velocity.

H2 Positive-energy class (sec 3.1, p.9): spherical symmetry -- an SO(3) whose orbits are orthogonal to xi -- which B-M state is possible 'only for class I and IV spacetimes, i.e., subluminal warp drives'.

H3 'Positive energy' means the energy density w in the comoving/Eulerian frame (eq 6, sec 2.3); no evaluation for all timelike observers, no NEC/DEC/SEC check on the pages read. Santiago-Schuster-Visser (2105.03079 p.11) state the Eulerian density 'is the only quantity Bobrick-Martire explicitly calculate'.

H4 Matter in D_warp an isotropic fluid with barotropic rho = rho(P) and P = 0 at inner and outer boundaries (p.10, eqs 8-9) -- the premise of N(r_in) = N(r_out) and hence 'time can only pass more slowly'.
H5 The only interior modification reachable with purely positive energy (spherical case) is slower interior time (p.18); axisymmetric positive-energy metrics are an open question (p.18).
H6 'Physical' is qualified: 'at least in principle' (abstract), 'our work suggests' (p.19); no explicit shell with all energy conditions verified is constructed.

H7 Optimisations (sec 5.3, A.3) act on the Alcubierre metric, whose Eulerian energy stays negative-definite; the factor ~3 is 'for a similarly sized Alcubierre drive', found 'numerically', comparison parameters not stated on the pages read; flattening's E -> E/alpha_X law (p.14, sec 4.1-4.2; derivation pages 11-13 NOT READ).
H8 Superluminal drives 'may always violate weak energy conditions' -- 'an established fact (Olum 1998, Visser et al. 2000)' (p.18); B-M's own argument for it is not a strict proof (p.18).

Symbolic (sympy): (1) eq 6-7: w = m'(r)/(4 pi r^2) -- positive Eulerian density <=> enclosed mass increasing; Lambda_out = 1/(1-2M/r) > 1 for M > 0; truncation lemma Int 4 pi r^2 w dr = m(r_out) - m(0) so a flat exterior forces sign-changing w. (2) eq 9: with rho = rho(P) and P = 0 at both faces, Int dP/(P+rho(P)) = 0 => N(r_in) = N(r_out). (3) A.6 -> A.7: angular integral 4/3 gives -(v^2/12) r^2 f'^2; integrand nonpositive for every real f' -- the SIGN claim of WARP-DRIVE.md:213 holds identically, shape and flattening rescale |E| only. (4) A.8: Euler-Lagrange (r^2 f')' = 0 -> f = C1 + C2/r; E_min = -(v^2/12) r0. (5) Flattening x' = alpha x: integrand form-invariant, Jacobian 1/alpha, E -> E/alpha (B-M p.14, p.18). Numeric (mpmath): (6) E_Alcubierre(tanh)/E_opt(r0 = R) = 0.77, 1.36, 2.68, 3.01, 6.67, 33.3 at sigma R = 2, 4, 8, 9, 20, 100 -> B-M's 'about a factor of three' is reproduced near sigma R = 8-9 and is parameter-dependent; for the tree's piecewise-linear 1 m wall at R = 100 m the ratio is 100.5. (7) Tree's 0.564 Msun and 0.019 Msun recomputed (0.56435, 0.01881); B-M optimum at r0 = 99.5 m is 0.0056 Msun, 0.00056 with /10 flattening -- the tree's figure is conservative by x33.8. (8) B-M p.10 Earth-mass 10 m shell: GM/(Rc^2) = 4.435e-4 vs printed 4e-4 (agrees). (9) RECORDED, source-internal: a constant-density isotropic hollow shell integrated outward from P(r_in) = 0 has P(r_out) < 0 for 2M/r_out from 0.003 to 0.73 -- B-M's isotropic 'P = 0 at inner and outer boundary' premise (H4) has no constant-density realisation; it needs tension zones, anisotropic stress, or a non-constant rho(P). Not a refutation: the conclusion (interior clocks slow inside a positive-mass shell) is also reached for a thin shell by continuity of g_tt, and the tree does not use eq 9. Not checkable here: whether any B-M sec-3 shell satisfies DEC/SEC (B-M give no explicit profile), and the flattening-law derivation on unread pp.11-13 (re-derived independently in (5)).

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. What B-M had in 2020-21: the Alcubierre/Natario literature, Olum 1998 and Visser et al. 2000 on superluminal WEC violation, Pfenning-Ford and Ford-Roman QIs -- and only the Eulerian energy density of their metrics (H3). What came later: (a) SSV 2021/22's generic NEC theorem for the Natario class and its demand that all T_ij be computed; (b) Warp Factory (Helmerich et al. 2024), the numerical toolkit for all-observer energy conditions; (c) Fuchs et al. 2024's shell with shift checked against NEC/WEC/DEC/SEC; (d) BBV 2026's critique. None of these is a measured datum; they are methods and constructions. Effect on the conclusion the tree uses: they CONFIRM it -- B-M did not verify the full energy conditions, the all-EC shell is Fuchs et al.'s, and it is subluminal. Evidence against 'lacked data' for this result: the missing ingredient was a calculation B-M could have done (all stress components), not a datum unavailable in 2021; SSV make exactly that point (p.16). Evidence for caution in M's favour of re-examination: B-M's sec-3 positive-energy premise (isotropic fluid, P = 0 at both faces) has no constant-density realisation (computed here), so their class is less explicit than their abstract suggests -- a gap in the derivation, not a missing datum, and it does not reverse 'time slows inside' (thin-shell junction). No datum moves any figure the tree takes from B-M: the tree's 0.564 -> 0.019 Msun is data-stable (G, Msun unchanged) and, if anything, conservative by x34 against B-M's own optimum.
grade_evidence: The two narrowings the owner makes (warpfolder.py:145-147) are READ at source and confirmed: B-M 2021 compute only the Eulerian density (their eq 6; SSV p.11; BBV Error 28) and claim no NEC/DEC/SEC verification, while Fuchs et al. 2024 claim the first subluminal constant-velocity solution satisfying NEC, WEC, DEC and SEC; B-M's positive-energy class is subluminal by construction (sec 3.1, 'only for class I and IV ... subluminal'). The owner's quoted sign claim (WARP-DRIVE.md:213) is machine-checked: E = -(v^2/12) Int r^2 f'^2 dr is nonpositive for every real f, so B-M's Alcubierre optimisations move the magnitude and not the sign. No datum moves anything. Recorded, not repaired, and not grounds for a lower grade because none reverses the owner's conclusion: (a) the rebuttal understates B-M -- B-M DO present a subluminal positive-(Eulerian-)energy spherical class (abstract, sec 3, p.19), which the folder's phrase reproduces, and the line-213 quotation addresses the Alcubierre optimisations instead; (b) WARP-DRIVE.md:208-211 imports B-M's 'about a factor of three' as fixed, whereas it is (sigma R)/3 and 100.5 for the tree's own 1 m-wall case -- the tree's 0.019 Msun is conservative by x33.8, against M; (c) WARP-DRIVE.md:352/:623 cite Fuchs as CQG 41 095009, which Fuchs's own ref [11] assigns to Helmerich et al.; (d) a source-internal gap -- B-M's isotropic 'P = 0 at both faces' premise has no constant-density realisation -- which the tree does not use.
